In this week, we will seek to understand the diversity of life in the sea. Who lives there? How are they related to one another? What traits define innovations that allow for the diversity we see. This week sets out the cast of characters we will seek to understand throughout the rest of the semester.

## 🧠🐛❓ Would you like to know more?

Want to read the classics on bottom-up control of salt marshes? There are a lot! See the classic - [@odumCOMPARISONPOPULATIONENERGY1959](https://files.celp-lab.org/biol311/readings/marsh/Odum%20and%20Smalley%20-%201959%20-%20Comparison%20of%20population%20energy%20flow%20of%20a%20herbivorous%20and%20a%20deposit-feeding%20invertebrate%20in%20a%20salt%20m.pdf),  [@tealEnergyFlowSalt1962](https://files.celp-lab.org/biol311/readings/marsh/Teal%20-%201962%20-%20Energy%20Flow%20in%20the%20Salt%20Marsh%20Ecosystem%20of%20Georgia.pdf), [@redfieldDevelopmentNewEngland1972](https://files.celp-lab.org/biol311/readings/marsh/Redfield%20-%201972%20-%20Development%20of%20a%20New%20England%20Salt%20Marsh.pdf), and [@nixonEcologyNewEngland1973a](https://files.celp-lab.org/biol311/readings/marsh/Nixon%20and%20Oviatt%20-%201973%20-%20Ecology%20of%20a%20New%20England%20Salt%20Marsh.pdf)

For how that might propogate up the brown web in marshes, see [@stivenResponseTwoSalt1979](https://files.celp-lab.org/biol311/readings/marsh/Stiven%20and%20Kuenzler%20-%201979%20-%20The%20Response%20of%20Two%20Salt%20Marsh%20Molluscs,%20Littorina%20irrorata%20and%20Geukensia%20demissa,%20to%20Field%20Manipula.pdf).

With respect to nutrients, Ivan Valiela at the MBL in Woods Hole has written some of the seminal classic work - see [@valielaNitrogenBudgetSalt1979](https://files.celp-lab.org/biol311/readings/marsh/Valiela%20and%20Teal%20-%201979%20-%20The%20nitrogen%20budget%20of%20a%20salt%20marsh%20ecosystem.pdf)

To get an update, and see how microbes play into the whole story, see [@bowenSaltMarshNitrogen2024](https://files.celp-lab.org/biol311/readings/marsh/Bowen_et_al_2023.pdf)

For the classic on positive interactions in marsh plants, see [@bertnessPhysicalStressPositive1994a](https://files.celp-lab.org/biol311/readings/marsh/Bertness%20and%20Hacker%20-%201994%20-%20Physical%20Stress%20and%20Positive%20Associations%20Among%20Marsh%20Plants.pdf) and then a followup in the upper marsh and more brackish systems with [@hackerExperimentalEvidenceFactors1999a](https://files.celp-lab.org/biol311/readings/marsh/Hacker%20and%20Bertness%20-%201999%20-%20Experimental%20Evidence%20for%20Factors%20Maintaining%20Plant%20Species%20Diversity%20in%20a%20New%20England%20Salt%20Marsh.pdf)

For the great synthesis of positive interactions and stress, see [@bertnessPositiveInteractionsCommunities1994](https://files.celp-lab.org/biol311/readings/marsh/Bertness%20and%20Callaway%20-%201994%20-%20Positive%20interactions%20in%20communities.pdf)

To learn more about the tight coupling between ribbed mussels and cordgrass, see [@bertnessRibbedMusselsSpartina1984a](https://files.celp-lab.org/biol311/readings/marsh/Bertness%20-%201984%20-%20Ribbed%20Mussels%20and%20Spartina%20Alterniflora%20Production%20in%20a%20New%20England%20Salt%20Marsh.pdf) and then followups such as [@angeliniKeystoneMutualismUnderpins2016](https://files.celp-lab.org/biol311/readings/marsh/Angelini%20et%20al.%20-%202016%20-%20A%20keystone%20mutualism%20underpins%20resilience%20of%20a%20coastal%20ecosystem%20to%20drought.pdf) and [@angeliniFoundationSpeciesOverlap2015a](https://files.celp-lab.org/biol311/readings/marsh/Angelini%20et%20al.%20-%202015%20-%20Foundation%20species'%20overlap%20enhances%20biodiversity%20and%20multifunctionality%20from%20the%20patch%20to%20landscape.pdf).

If you want to learn more about top-down control in salt marses, see [@sillimanTopdownControlSpartina2001](https://files.celp-lab.org/biol311/readings/marsh/Silliman%20and%20Zieman%20-%202001%20-%20Top-down%20Control%20of%20Spartina%20Alterniflora%20Production%20by%20Periwinkle%20Grazing%20in%20a%20Virginia%20Salt%20Marsh.pdf) and a followup [@sillimanTrophicCascadeRegulates2002](https://files.celp-lab.org/biol311/readings/marsh/Silliman%20and%20Bertness%20-%202002%20-%20A%20trophic%20cascade%20regulates%20salt%20marsh%20primary%20production.pdf) for the trophic cascade. For then a big review, see [@heConsumerControlCommon2016](https://files.celp-lab.org/biol311/readings/marsh/He%20and%20Silliman%20-%202016%20-%20Consumer%20control%20as%20a%20common%20driver%20of%20coastal%20vegetation%20worldwide.pdf).

When we get into modern human impacts, check out the classic review [@gedanCenturiesHumandrivenChange2009](https://files.celp-lab.org/biol311/readings/marsh/Gedan_et_al_2009.pdf) - and if you want to get more specific, a few pieces to consider:
     - Eutrophication can cause marsh slumping and break up, from [@deeganCoastalEutrophicationDriver2012](https://files.celp-lab.org/biol311/readings/marsh/Deegan_et_al_2012.pdf)  
     - If fishing removes predators of herbivorous marsh crabs, this can lead to large-scale defaunation. [@altieriTrophicCascadeTriggers2012](https://files.celp-lab.org/biol311/readings/marsh/Altieri%202012%20Ecology.pdf).  
     - Sea level rise is also of critical importance - see [@kirwanTidalWetlandStability2013](https://files.celp-lab.org/biol311/readings/marsh/Kirwan%202013%20Nature.pdf).
